Here are the seven defining constants from the BIPM “The International System of Units (SI): Defining constants” page, in the order displayed in the seven-row table, with each symbol, exact numerical value, and SI unit preserved exactly as shown:

1) Caesium hyperfine frequency
- Name: caesium hyperfine frequency
- Symbol: ΔνCs
- Exact numerical value: 9 192 631 770
- SI unit: Hz

2) Speed of light in vacuum
- Name: speed of light in vacuum
- Symbol: c
- Exact numerical value: 299 792 458
- SI unit: m s–1

3) Planck constant
- Name: Planck constant
- Symbol: h
- Exact numerical value: 6.626 070 15 x 10–34
- SI unit: J s

4) Elementary charge
- Name: elementary charge
- Symbol: e
- Exact numerical value: 1.602 176 634 x 10–19
- SI unit: C

5) Boltzmann constant
- Name: Boltzmann constant
- Symbol: k
- Exact numerical value: 1.380 649 x 10–23
- SI unit: J K–1

6) Avogadro constant
- Name: Avogadro constant
- Symbol: NA
- Exact numerical value: 6.022 140 76 x 1023
- SI unit: mol–1

7) Luminous efficacy of a defined visible radiation
- Name: luminous efficacy of a defined visible radiation
- Symbol: Kcd
- Exact numerical value: 683
- SI unit: lm W–1

Statement about the uncertainty of these numerical values (from the page text):
- “It is by fixing the exact numerical value of each that the unit becomes defined, since the product of the numerical value and the unit must equal the value of the constant.”

This statement implies that the numerical values of the defining constants are fixed exactly (i.e. they carry no uncertainty), and the units are defined so that the product of each fixed numerical value with its SI unit equals the corresponding constant.
